messages:
Carla (Support): heads up — ticket from Acme: sudden 502/503s hitting hosted API since the 07:40 deploy. customer says their app started failing around 07:42 PST.
Ben (Oncall): seeing it on grafana — error rate up on /v1/generate, p95 latency + timeouts. Canary is at 10%.
Alice (SRE): canary id? did we flip any routing flags in the deploy?
Dave (Runtime): canary=canary-202403. We rolled kernelv2/quantized path and a config change earlier. I pushed `feature.kvcache_v2=true` to the canary selector.
Carla (Support): customer sent a minimal repro — curl returns 502. They include an X-Client-Auth header.
Carla (Support): ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Auth: aws:org-123" https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Ben (Oncall): gateway logs show `upstream timeout` and `invalid auth header` logs being turned into 502s for some requests. sample trace id: 4f3a9b2c.
Alice (SRE): checking config registry — looks like the canary selection accidentally used `authority: global` instead of `authority: seed`. That would cause the auth transform to be applied cluster-wide for canary backends.
Dave (Runtime): yup that matches: the auth header sanitizer has a special-case for tenant-bound routes that we expected to be seed-scoped; with global authority enabled it mutated headers for regular traffic routed through canary machines. Bad interaction with edge proxy -> downstream 502s/timeouts.
Frank (CS): customer impact = high. They're seeing repeated failures. Need rollback and a comms update.
Ben (Oncall): initiating rollback to 0% canary now — want to avoid toggle oscillation. tagging infra pager.
deploy-bot: Rollback started: canary-202403 10% -> 0% (initiated by Ben). ETA ~ 30s.
Ben (Oncall): command run: `./deployctl set-canary --id=canary-202403 --percent=0`
Ben (Oncall): also patching the config so the `authority` field won't accept `global` in canary selector.
Alice (SRE): monitoring... canary machines are being drained from router. watch logs for residual auth 502s.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 07:52 PST. canary traffic now 0%.
Ben (Oncall): error rate dropping, p95 back to baseline after ~90s. partial customer successes reported. :thumbsup:
Carla (Support): customer confirms intermittent success, some requests still get 502 but much reduced.
Alice (SRE): TTL on config sync is ~90s; some hosts still had mutated behavior until they refreshed. expect fully recovered in 2m.
Dave (Runtime): root cause = human config selector mistake in the canary PR (authority scope wrong) + missing validation that allowed global authority on canary selector. will open follow-up PR to add validation and a deploy-time lint. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567
Frank (CS): will update customer with ETA and postmortem note.
Ben (Oncall): postmortem action items: 1) add server-side lint to reject `authority: global` in canary selectors unless explicitly flagged; 2) add guardrail in console to warn on non-seed-scoped flags; 3) audit recent canary configs for similar mistakes; 4) run a small chaos test to ensure auth transform isolation.
Alice (SRE): also adding runbook step to pause canary if 5xx>threshold for 5m automatically instead of manual only.
Dave (Runtime): I'll revert the canary PR and push validation today. file: runtimes/selector-validation.
Carla (Support): good — I'll keep ticket updated and confirm with Acme once stable.
Ben (Oncall): thanks everyone. closing timeline: deploy @07:40 -> spike at 07:42 -> rollback @07:51 -> recovery by 07:53-07:54.
Carla (Support): :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: incident-channel-note: follow-up required, create incident doc and assign owners.
Dave (Runtime): filing incident doc now, linking PR.
Ben (Oncall): follow-up owners: Dave (runtime), Alice (sre), Carla (support), Frank (cs).
Carla (Support): tagging this for postmortem.
